chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Mūsā ibn Saʿdān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: The nose and the mouth do not become junub, because they are passages through which fluid passes.

key_terms.الْأَنْفُ: the nose, mentioned here in the context of ritual purity
key_terms.الْفَمُ: the mouth, mentioned here in the context of ritual purity
key_terms.سَائِلَانِ: two flowing passages; channels through which fluid passes
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: to render in a state of janabah or impurity

ai.seo_question: Do the mouth and nose become junub, making rinsing them obligatory in ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning janabah and the status of the mouth and nose. It indicates that they are not treated as becoming junub in themselves, because they are flowing passages, which relates to the fiqh discussion of rinsing the mouth and drawing water into the nose.
